cells.tense: You can see the whole shape of the thing and you are working it right here.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about something you made or fixed this week, then let it count as finished.
cells.core: You can see how a thing works without getting lost in the details, and when something pulls you off center you find the pattern underneath it and steady yourself with it. That's the whole trick and it's running right now.\n\nThere's a fairness in how you handle people that doesn't need checking. You feel what's owed and what's right, and you don't spend hours arguing yourself into it. Keep it that way by saying plainly what you've done and letting it stand, the way other people's work stands. The calm isn't the reward for the gathering; it's what the gathering feels like while it's going.
cells.sheetLine: You find the pattern, and fairness follows without a fight.

cells.tense: You're ahead of where the day actually is, bracing for an answer not yet arrived.
cells.ask: Act on one thing you genuinely want, finish it, then let the next one wait until tomorrow.
cells.core: You're trying to line up every scattered thought before you move, like the plan has to be whole in your head or it doesn't count. So you keep sorting, waiting for a version that arrives finished. The day passes and the thing you actually care about hasn't had one honest step.\n\nThe gathering isn't the problem; the rush past the present is. The ground comes back when you let the feeling under the stack say what matters, and you start from there. One piece, chosen because you want it, acted on today. The rest can wait till morning without turning into a threat.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing the pieces together before you've heard what matters.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed some time behind you.
cells.ask: Sit with what you know you want for five quiet minutes, then write one sentence of what surfaced.
cells.core: You can see the shape of your own life clearly enough. What's gone is the pull of it, the warmth that used to make a choice matter. When this is working, you gather what matters and it settles into a line you can walk — not perfect, but yours, and it carries you through the day. Lately the gathering happens and nothing lands. No choice weighs much either way.\n\nFeeling doesn't come back through force. Try sitting with what you already want, quietly, without asking it to decide anything tomorrow. What you find might be small. Write it down anyway. The pattern holds more once some feeling is back in the room with it.

cells.tense: You're already living the pattern, and still describing it as if it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Show one thing you've worked out to another person, and let them use it their own way.
cells.core: You already handle the scatter better than you admit. Your days have a shape and you keep it, and that shape is something you built. But when it's described back to you, it sounds like something that just happened, or like a rule you follow, not like your own arrangement.\n\nThe pattern is yours and quiet. It doesn't need credit to keep working. But over time, not owning it makes it smaller than it is. Say out loud to one person that you arranged a piece of your life and you're glad you did. Not as a boast. As a plain fact.
